parts:
hi Leo,
 This model has a constant detection probability model which is why the predictions are the same for all sites.  You have a different lambda value because you modeled camera as an effect on lambda.   You should model it also as an effect on detection if you want to evaluate that.
regards
andy

Hi Andy,

my data is from a 1500m camera transect with camera sites every 100m. At each camera site I have 4 different cameras. Using the above method I have obtained detection probability estimates for single cameras of each camera type across the 1500m transect (below). I then pooled the data from the first and second camera site, the third and fourth camera site, etc (pooled separately for different camera types) and recalculated detection probability. I continued to pool data over 3, 4, 5 cameras, etc. However, in some cases detection probability estimates from the pooled data decreased. I presume this is because I am doing something wrong? I was expecting that detection probability estimates could only ever increase or remain the same if I pooled data across multiple cameras. Thanks in advance.

> m1 <- occuRN(~camera ~1,pilot)

> est.det.prob <- predict(m1,type = 'det',newdata=siteCovs,appendData=TRUE)
